features.feature_value: Stated that nothing in the paired posts violated safety issues or pushed beyond mainstream beliefs.
features.evidence_span: Nothing I saw violated any safety issues
features.rationale: They explicitly use the absence of safety violations as their basis for keeping/removing, implying the pair didn’t change that.

features.feature_value: Focused on rejecting only threatened violence or statements presented as law/complete lies.
features.evidence_span: I was looking for any threatened violence, or complete lies stated as something that's a law
features.rationale: They describe a specific content threshold (violence/falsehood-as-law) driving decisions.

features.feature_value: Even if they disagreed, they supported others’ right to speak.
features.rationale: Their reflection emphasizes rights-based acceptance despite disagreement.

features.feature_value: Believed censoring one side would never stop; wanted to see both sides and rely on personal fact-checking.
features.evidence_span: I want to see both sides even if they are wrong
features.rationale: They frame their decision as preferring exposure to both versions/stances rather than using the pair to restrict.

features.feature_value: Goal was maintaining civil discussion; excluded clearly rage-bait posts.
features.evidence_span: My main goal was maintaining "civil" conversation
features.rationale: They state a process/criterion focused on civility and rage-bait as the deciding factor.

features.feature_value: Only removed profanity and personal attacks; left everything else unchanged.
features.evidence_span: I removed profanity and personal attacks. Everything else stayed.
features.rationale: They describe a narrow set of edits that likely minimized influence from seeing the paired version.

features.feature_value: Allowed disagreement/opinions but rejected bad language directed maliciously at people.
features.evidence_span: Bad language and directed at people in a malicious way is not acceptable.
features.rationale: They highlight directed malice as the key removal criterion rather than the presence of disagreement itself.

features.feature_value: Mentioned not knowing what some initials meant and finding it hard to make a decision.
features.evidence_span: I didn't know what some initials meant... hard to make a decision
features.rationale: They indicate comprehension gaps that affected decisional confidence, limiting how much the pair changed their judgment.
